top_story: Israel’s largest air campaign of the war struck more than 100 sites across Lebanon within minutes on 8 April, killing at least 254 people and wounding more than 1,100, with the scale and speed of the attack deepening civilian trauma and sharply raising the risk of wider escalation. By 9 April, Beirut moved to reassert political control over any diplomatic track, with the prime minister publicly rejecting Iranian negotiation on Lebanon’s behalf as the strikes exposed both Lebanon’s vulnerability and the sensitivity of outside influence. The combination of mass civilian casualties and Lebanon’s insistence on sovereign decision-making points to a dual crisis: an immediate humanitarian shock and a tightening contest over who speaks for Lebanon under fire. The clearest near-term implication is that Israeli military pressure is not only widening the battlefield but also reshaping the political terms of any ceasefire effort.
